rationale: Evidence from the only raced design (iteration 2): 0 of 60 trials finished. Every run ended off track, at progress 0.22 on the oval, 0.04 on the s-bend and 0.035 on the slalom. rms_error (0.025 to 0.03 m) is well inside the 0.06 m limit, but max_error sits at about 0.06 m, so the robot is making sharp excursions and leaving the tape rather than drifting slowly. The oval is the gentlest track and still fails at 21% progress, which points to a systematic bias plus overshoot rather than sharp-bend failure alone. The fixed left/right motor mismatch is the likely bias, and with ki = 0 the controller carries a steady offset into every run. Off-track limit check: max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, and widening the body to 0.18 only reaches 0.0575 m, so body_width cannot buy margin and I leave it at 0.12. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.4 to 1.3, so the robot has more time to react in bends. Finishing (500 points) is worth far more than speed, and the 3 s limit is a looser constraint than staying on the line. (2) kp 3.0 to 3.5, for stronger correction of the motor-mismatch drift. (3) ki 0.0 to 0.3, to cancel the steady bias; the integral is bounded at +/-2, so windup risk is small. (4) kd 0.5 to 0.8, to damp the overshoot that causes the max_error spikes. Geometry is otherwise unchanged, so the race isolates the controller effect. Expected result: fewer off-track exits, more progress on all three tracks (target above 0.5 on the oval), and possibly the first finishes. Main risk: the higher kd may amplify sensor noise, which the race should show in steering_oscillation.
